questions.stem: Two FGCP peers show out-of-sync; only WWAN IPv6 differs and heartbeat counters are healthy. What is safest?

choices.text: Compare each modem-learned address and document the exception; avoid checksum recalculation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Force a full resync immediately and clear every checksum difference.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run checksum recalculation on both members before checking modem state.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable heartbeat monitoring so the dashboard no longer reports drift.

questions.explanation: The dynamic cellular address explains this documented false-positive checksum mismatch; recalculation can overwrite the peer address.
questions.source_url: Recalculation is specifically discouraged because the modem-learned address can be overwritten on the peer.

questions.source_url: The counters support healthy heartbeat and monitored-interface paths; they do not prove checksum equality.

questions.stem: A different non-WWAN table appears after an upgrade and a controlled change fails to propagate. What next?

questions.explanation: Recalculate checksums before collecting the table name or member status.

questions.stem: Why should an operator avoid `diagnose ha checksum recalculate` for the documented WWAN mismatch?

choices.feedback: It disables the secondary heartbeat interface until the next election.
